Define Node and .NET specific profiles and associated toolchain
Extend repository intelligence to recognize .NET solution/project markers
Implement precise dependency preparation with immutable package-domain allowlist
Define clear rules for repository intelligence extension and server-owned validation profiles
Design Bounded Dependency Preparation for offline validation without network access
Ensure security requirements for PREPARE network authority
Implement Acceptance Criteria for all major validations
Create Scope and Non-Goals for expected implementation areas
Define Release Gate for exact release deployment and validation

Update W8-S2 OT Time production replay with new validation profile and pre-materialization authorization-envelope validation

validations: Ensure Python/Node/.NET compatibility evidence is deterministic and does not execute or trust repository command text
Verify fixed server-owned toolchain profiles contain only server-owned command templates
Ensure deterministic fail-closed selection for .NET validation
Implement Python behavior does not regress by validating existing Python/Parallax fixtures
Verify Node remains bounded by validating a representative Node repository
Implement Candidate and canonical validation agree by comparing selected profile identity to candidate-validation evidence and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY
Ensure Dependency/toolchain readiness fails closed by validating missing executable, failed PREPARE, inability to lock the network to deny-all, or unavailable dependency

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Repository intelligence recognizes representative `.sln`, `.csproj`, and C# source evidence deterministically, records bounded evidence identities, and does not execute or trust repository command text.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Python, Node, and .NET profiles contain only server-owned command templates. Repository/model/user text cannot change executable, argument template, environment, network, provider, Git, deployment, or approval authority.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — An exact source tree produces one stable profile/root identity or a typed unsupported/ambiguous result. Mixed/conflicting roots never trigger guessed execution.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A representative OT Time-like C# repository selects the .NET profile; dependency preparation uses only fixed `dotnet restore` with the exact NuGet domain allowlist; candidate BUILD/TEST/VERIFY then use fixed offline `dotnet` invocations against the admitted solution/project identity instead of Parallax pytest paths.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Representative existing Python/Parallax fixtures retain the exact established protected BUILD/TEST/VERIFY behavior and all inherited execution-policy tests remain green. Generic Python repositories are not silently admitted through broadened commands.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — A representative Node repository is either validated through a fixed admitted Node profile or explicitly rejected when safe fixed commands cannot be proven. Repository `scripts` values never become command authority.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — The selected validation profile identity is bound to candidate-validation evidence and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY; canonical execution cannot silently switch profile/toolchain after candidate admission.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Missing executable, failed PREPARE, inability to lock the network to deny-all, or unavailable dependency returns bounded non-success evidence and performs no source-lineage acceptance, Git/provider mutation, deployment mutation, or fabricated lifecycle progress.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Project/spec/run identity, single-writer source acceptance, immutable lineage, evaluator precedence, tenant/auth, source-only handoff, Vercel Preview delivery, provider scopes, and REVIEW boundaries do not regress. Spoofed stage specs remain rejected before accepted-lineage materialization.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — After exact release deployment, a QA-owned source-only Project bound to `github:Ryan9876/ot-time` progresses from PLAN through IMPLEMENT/BUILD/TEST/VERIFY to REVIEW and the authenticated exact-lineage ZIP handoff verifies, without Vercel deployment target, Vercel repository-provider authorization, out-of-band source edit, owner impersonation, or DB mutation.
risks: Material risk of arbitrary repository script execution
Unrestricted network access during dependency preparation
Injecting package-manager credentials or private-feed secrets in this slice
Replacing Vercel Sandbox in this slice
Supporting every language/toolchain in one release

critique: The specification provides a clear objective to generalize protected candidate and accepted-lineage validation for Parallax applications using deterministic server-owned command profiles selected from bounded repository evidence. The fixed decisions include repository compatibility evidence and executable command authority, as well as server-owned validation profiles and bounded dependency preparation.
